<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with disciplined, source-free but plausible reasoning, and both met the Q/A format cleanly. CON (A) landed two genuinely damaging hits: the coercion-symmetry point (opt-in simply migrates take-it-or-leave-it from page 34 to the audition) and the enforcement point (signatures do not self-enforce; a breached opt-in lands in the same unaffordable litigation PRO decried), plus a real cost/holdout story about niche and catalog localization. But PRO (B) answered both honestly and with a distinction that survived: a discrete, dated, scoped, priced grant is a *visible* and therefore governable term, and the nudity-rider analogy showed nobody responds to audition pressure by folding a term back into boilerplate. More importantly, PRO turned CON's own alternative: every mechanism CON praises — disclosure, use limits, revocation, guild floors, the recent negotiated digital-replica terms — presupposes that the studio needs something the performer has not already conveyed. CON's reply that bargained floors can exist without a consent default was the thinnest part of its case, and "enforcement of what? you cannot police a use nobody was entitled to refuse" left CON's enforcement symmetry argument blunted. CON also had to defend broad boilerplate specifically, and its retreat to "negotiated contracting" partly conceded PRO's default-entitlement frame. PRO additionally neutralized the holdout/veto scare by supplying a concrete fallback (the century-old human dubber) and reframing CON's cost objection as a margin interest rather than an audience interest, while CON's counter-claim that a shrunken market employs fewer dubbers stayed asserted rather than established. Clear but competitive win for PRO.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's answer to the coercion-symmetry pressure — conceding that opt-in, like nudity riders, becomes a condition of casting, but insisting a visible, dated, scoped, priced term can be bargained, sunset and regulated while a 2019 clause cannot — combined with "you cannot bargain over what the other side already owns." That pairing absorbed CON's best attack and converted CON's own collective-bargaining alternative into a reason to vote PRO.</best_rebuttal>
